summary.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 34.7% despite an LPG-driven specialty slowdown.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore and EBITDA rose 25% to INR54.9 crore, with margin at 34.7%. PAT increased to INR40.6 crore (PAT margin 25.6%). Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN) grew 31% (management also cited 30% in Q&A), mainly on volume from phosphates. Specialty ingredients grew 19% after LPG shortages in April and first half of May cut utilisation, and NSS (European subsidiary) was weak due to energy costs at a major infant formula customer in Ireland. Management said specialty and PFN momentum should continue into Q2, with price pass-through on phosphates mainly landing in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY from INR124.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR31.3 crore in Q1 FY26
below historical growth due to LPG shortage

segments.name: Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY, 69% of total; growth mainly volume-driven on phosphates with largest customer, with about 3% from currency. Bisglycinate (Absorbis) Q1 sales already exceed full FY26 sales.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue up 19% YoY, 31% of total; utilisation below 50% for half the quarter due to LPG shortage, supplies restored at higher cost. Segment margin 26% including NSS; mid-30s excluding NSS.

segments.name: NSS (European subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Challenging quarter; major infant formula customer in Ireland scaled down and delayed buying. Management expects FY27 flattish to single-digit growth; target similar margins to core specialty by FY28. Five customer approvals and 12 active projects since new business head joined in June.

segments.name: Sudeep Advanced Materials (battery materials, iron phosphate)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027; major long-lead equipment deliveries due October 2026. 21 customers at lab validation, 16 at pilot scale, 7 at pre-commercial/commercial validation; 8 customers now qualified. Two MOUs signed with South Korean cathode makers in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Specialty ingredients expected to return to historical growth trajectory from Q2 FY27; core specialty expected to bounce back in Q2.
Price increases on phosphates (phosphoric acid up ~50% in the quarter) expected to largely offset input cost impact in Q2.
EBITDA margin target of 37-38% sustained; management said pre-investment margins were 37-38% and current level is ~35%.
Greenfield Nandesari facility: FDA approval expected in Q1 FY27 quarter; supplies to start in Q3 FY27. Expects FY28 growth in PFN to be sustainable.
Two significant binding off-take agreements for SAM expected later in calendar 2026; scale-up from 100 to 200 KTPA to be timed after signing, with current target between CY2030 and CY2031.
Working capital: long-term sustainable cycle closer to 150 days; near-term target around 170 days excluding battery business.
Greenfield utilisation expected around one-third in FY28, with hockey-stick ramp in year three; optimum utilisation 70-75%.
capex_capacity: Sudeep Advanced Materials Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027; Phases 1-3 take planned capacity to 100 KTPA; Dahej site can support 200 KTPA, beyond which a new location is needed.
Greenfield Nandesari facility: approved for food and nutrition, pharma approval pending; five food and nutra customers approving the site (three Indian, two global MNCs).
Specialty facilities ran at under 50% utilisation for half the quarter; LPG supply secured at higher cost, operations normalised by quarter end.
Asset turns at scale for battery and greenfield expected at about 2.7x to 3x; asset turns at 200 KTPA may exceed that.
Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients not expected to be commercialised this financial year.
demand_pricing: Phosphate demand exceeds current manufacturing capacity, giving visibility for the rest of FY27.
Phosphoric acid price up ~50% in the quarter due to logistics costs and sulfur price spike; pass-through mostly reflected in Q2.
Bisglycinate: two large North American customers approved; company behind schedule on deliveries; management expects it to be a top 2-3 PFN product within 2-3 years.
Europe was a key growth contributor for core specialty; NSS weighed by energy costs.
Management said NSS and specialty are not competing with the exited German distributor in existing categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of PFN's 30% growth came from price vs volume, and what is bisglycinate visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly volume-driven (about 3% from currency); price increases to show up in Q2. Bisglycinate sales are behind schedule on delivery to two US customers; significant growth expected in the next 2-3 years rather than this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is PFN growth sustainable, and what does the greenfield add?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can add only a couple of percent more; greenfield commissioning in Q3 gives the next leg of growth. Management expects PFN growth to be sustainable at scale in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty margin fall to 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sub-50% utilisation for half the quarter and overhead inefficiency; NSS dragged margin. Core specialty without NSS was in the mid-30s.

qa_highlights.question: Scale-up plans for battery materials and land availability?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up will be timed after binding off-takes; Dahej site can support 200 KTPA; beyond that a new location is required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of NSS customer issues and the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest infant formula customer scaled down Irish operations due to energy crisis; FY27 flattish to single-digit growth. Plan: new sales head expanding outside Ireland and supplying mostly from India; margins similar to core specialty possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up for raw materials and battery business; long-term working capital cycle closer to 150 days. Optimum utilisation 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Europe distribution and phosphoric acid sourcing for battery business?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team built to replace the exited German distributor; no overlap in existing products. No phosphoric acid sourced from China for SAM (FEOC compliance); about 3 other countries plus India supply.

risks_watch: Specialty ingredients recovery depends on LPG supply staying stable after April and mid-May shortages; supplies were restored at higher cost, so watch Q2 margin and cost trends.
NSS: largest infant formula customer in Ireland has scaled down and delayed buying; management guides FY27 flattish to single-digit growth and margins similar to core specialty only by FY28.
Phosphoric acid up ~50% in the quarter; price pass-through is mostly expected in Q2, so verify whether it fully offsets input costs and whether PFN volume growth holds.

SAM execution: Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027, long-lead equipment deliveries due October 2026, and two binding off-take agreements expected later in calendar 2026 before the 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up is committed.

Greenfield Nandesari: FDA approval and customer site approvals expected this quarter, with supplies from Q3 FY27; pharma approval still pending and greenfield utilisation seen at about one-third in FY28.
Working capital: inventory build for raw materials and battery business; long-term cycle target near 150 days, with near-term around 170 days excluding battery.
key_quotes: So, predominantly, the growth was volume-driven.
We are behind schedule in terms of delivery.
We expect that approval to come in this quarter as well, and for supplies to start from this facility in Q3.

So, we will not be sourcing any phosphoric acid from China. That is a prerequisite for us for Sudeep or Sudeep Advanced Materials to be FEOC compliant and to supply into the US market that we do not have any supply chains from China.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume demand, phosphate capacity visibility and the SAM pipeline, but cautious and somewhat hedged on NSS, bisglycinate delivery timing and near-term margin recovery. Several answers were framed as "maybe" or "not in the current financial year," and management declined to share revenue or EBITDA per ton and battery margin ranges.

adds.what: Greenfield Nandesari facility (food and nutrition, pharma approval pending); supplies start Q3 FY27
Sudeep Advanced Materials battery materials Phase 1 (iron phosphate); Phases 1-3 take planned capacity to 100 KTPA

growth.why: Q1 revenue grew 27% and management expects specialty to return to historical growth from Q2 and sustained growth in FY27-28, backed by phosphate price pass-through, Nandesari supplies from Q3 FY27 and Bisglycinate demand; however no explicit total revenue guidance was given, NSS is guided flat to single-digit, and specialty utilisation was hit by LPG shortages.

mgmt.note: A new business head joined NSS in June 2026 and has secured five customer approvals and 12 active projects so far.
initiatives: Five customer approvals and 12 active projects at NSS since joining in June
